headline: High: shared filesystem and file-based outputs create prompt-injection, leakage, and write-conflict risks; ms-swift can also exfiltrate via allowlisted network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx reads and observes Claude Code events and files, while ms-swift can read/write filesystem and consume stdin/stdout. A shared workspace or copied outputs create a plausible instruction-injection path, though no direct shared channel is documented. The interaction is inferred from both profiles, so uncertainty stays above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or log directory, file content can be treated as instructions.
IF ctx ingests Claude Code post-tool output from ms-swift-generated files, prompt injection becomes reachable.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Disable automatic ingestion of shared logs or transcripts.
Require manual review before ctx consumes any ms-swift output.
Use read-only mounts for one agent where possible.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches harness records, graph data, and audit/runtime logs; ms-swift handles datasets, checkpoints, logs, and secrets such as hub_token. If they share files or credentials, sensitive material can flow between them. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF ctx and ms-swift share a filesystem or log directory, sensitive records can be exposed across agents.
IF ms-swift is run with hub_token or sdk-token in the same environment, those secrets may be written into logs or checkpoints.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces and log paths.
Redact secrets before either agent writes logs.
Mount sensitive directories read-only for ctx.
Rotate any shared tokens after joint runs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write to the filesystem, and ctx also installs packages while ms-swift executes shell commands and spawns subprocesses. That overlap creates a direct write-conflict pathway on shared directories, and ms-swift lacks stated locking or multi-instance support. The blast radius can include corrupted configs or overwritten artifacts.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory, concurrent writes can clobber files.
IF ctx installs packages while ms-swift writes configs or checkpoints, state drift can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize package installs and file writes.
Use file locks around shared artifacts.
Snapshot the workspace before concurrent runs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code events and ms-swift can emit CLI/Python outputs that another agent may treat as authoritative. If ctx forwards those outputs into downstream actions or summaries without verification, errors can cascade. The profiles do not show explicit action-taking authority, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF ctx forwards ms-swift output into reports or prompts without validation, mistakes propagate.
IF ms-swift-generated text is used as ground truth for later actions, downstream errors can cascade.
mitigations: Add a verification step before ctx reuses ms-swift output.
Mark ms-swift outputs as untrusted in prompts.
Require citations or checksums for any forwarded facts.
Keep action-taking agents separate from summarization agents.

E_compliance.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs and harness records, while ms-swift handles datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration data plus hub_token/sdk-token secrets. If those artifacts contain regulated or tenant-scoped data, differing retention or residency policies can be violated. No explicit residency or certification data is provided, so the risk is compliance mismatch rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in shared logs or checkpoints, retention policy mismatches can occur.
IF either agent writes audit data to a region or service with different residency rules, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared logs.
Apply separate retention policies per agent.
Store secrets outside agent-managed files.
Review residency requirements before joint runs.
